medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
A student may not leave school prior to completion of an academic year unless granted a leave of absence by the Senior Associate Dean for Medical Education and Student Affairs. A student who leaves without such permission or who fails to return by the end of the granted term of leave is considered dismissed from the School of Medicine and may return only by applying for readmission. Typically only one leave of absence will be granted during a student's tenure at the School of Medicine. In an extreme circumstance and with the Dean's approval, an additional leave may be granted.Students may request a leave of absence for one of the following:
1) Medical/Health
2) Financial
3) Academic
4) Educational/Participation in a joint degree program
5) Personal/Other

Students must meet with the Senior Associate Dean for Medical Education and Students Affairs to request the leave; Documentation may be required prior to approval.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Office of Medical Education provides support for a variety of specialty interest groups, student governing bodies, intramural sports and other student organizations that enrich the learning environment while promoting student well-being. For more information on student organizations, please visit the following site:  https://medschool.vcu.edu/education/medical-education/supporting-our-students/student-organizations/
medSchoolStudLife.setting: As an urban academic medical center, the VCU School of Medicine rests in the heart of Richmond, Virginia — affectionately known as RVA to those who live here. We pride ourselves on being active members of our community, with a commitment to engaging and investing in Richmond as learners, researchers, healers and citizens. For more information regarding RVA, please visit the following site: https://medschool.vcu.edu/about-richmond/
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Limited single student housing is available on the Monroe Park campus for graduate and professional students. Off-campus housing is plentiful, varied in style, and reasonable in cost. For more information on off-campus housing, please visit the following site: https://offcampus.vcu.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Within the Office of Medical Education, our Student Affairs and Student Engagement team members coordinate resources to support the personal and professional identity development of all medical students while attending VCU School of Medicine.For more information about service provided, please visit the following site: https://medschool.vcu.edu/education/medical-education/supporting-our-students/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The VCU Division for Academic Success works collaboratively with the Office of Medical Education to provide disability and academic support services to medical students. For more information on their services, please visit the following site: https://das.vcu.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Within the Office of Medical Education, our Student Affairs and Student Engagement team members coordinate resources to support the personal and professional identity development of all medical students while attending VCU School of Medicine. Using the greater university RamStrong model,  activities and resources are designed to promote the eight dimensions of well-being: emotional, environmental, financial, intellectual, occupational, physical, social, and spiritual. University Counseling Services and Student Health both have offices located on the Health Science Campus and often participate in workshops and seminars focused on personal well-being.
For more information about service provided by the Office of Medical Education, please visit the following site: https://medschool.vcu.edu/education/medical-education/supporting-our-students/
For more information about resources available to the entire VCU community, please visit the following site: https://ramstrong.vcu.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: From academic support services and career advising to student well-being initiatives, the Office of Medical Education has dedicated deans and staff members ready to help medical students navigate their medical education experience at VCU School of Medicine. The Medical College of Virginia campus houses other health professional schools including Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, and the College of Health Professions creating a collaborative learning environment for students from each program. For more information on the VCU Health Science Campus, please visit the following site: https://www.vcu.edu/programs/colleges-and-schools/
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students must have access to reliable transportation for all clinical experiences including preceptorship for the M1/M2 Practice of Clinical Medicine longitudinal course and M3/M4 clinical experiences as we use a variety of clinical sites in Central Virginia and throughout the state.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Over the course of four years, students build on foundational knowledge, develop core clinical skills and explore specialty areas under the guidance of some of the top providers in their fields. Longitudinal curriculum throughout the program ensures active learning through the lenses of professionalism, humanism, and compassionate, patient-centered care.

The fall semester of M1, known as the Scientific Foundations of Medicine phase, emphasizes foundational knowledge required to understand the structure, function and pathophysiology of the different organ systems. During the Applied Medical Sciences phase that spans the spring semester of M1 and the fall semester of M2, students study each organ system block covering normal anatomy and physiology before delving into disease diagnosis, pathophysiology and management.

After completion of the Applied Medical Sciences phase, students spend 6-8 dedicated weeks preparing for the NBME Step 1 exam with close guidance from a faculty adviser on effective study plans and resources.

During the M3 year, students receive clinical training by rotating through eight core clerkships located at various hospitals and ambulatory services, including VCU Health, Richmond Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center, Riverside Regional Medical Center and other community-based health care facilities throughout Virginia.

M4 is a year of advanced clinical concentrations, consisting of 40 weeks of elective rotations and eight weeks of acting internships tailored to support career goals. Students also complete a required four-week clerkship in Emergency Medicine and are given up to four weeks of dedicated time to study for the NBME Step 2 CK exam.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
VCU School of Medicine’s mission is to improve health through exceptional and innovative discovery, training and patient care. VCU Health is central Virginia’s only academic medical center and the largest single provider of indigent health care in the commonwealth. Students are exposed to primary care throughout all four years of the curriculum, from working with primary care small group leaders in the Practice of Clinical Medicine longitudinal course to clerkship/elective experiences in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, and Pediatrics. Interested students can participate in para-curricular programs including:
•	FM Stat – designed to nurture, develop, and support medical students who express an interest in a career as a Family Medicine physician.
•	I2CRP – designed to provide additional training, service, and clinical opportunities to students interested in working with underserved patient populations.

More information about research for medical students can be found here: https://medschool.vcu.edu/research/medical-students/

medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: While students are not required to participate in research or write a thesis as a graduation requirement, the vast majority participate in some type of research experience prior to graduation.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: VCU Health, Children’s Hospital of Richmond, Richmond Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center, Riverside Regional Medical Center, and other community-based health care facilities throughout Virginia.

medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Our mission is to improve health through exceptional and innovative discovery, training and patient care. With the help of our strategic plan, we will achieve our vision of being known for the accomplishments of our trainees, faculty, staff and alumni in research, education and patient care.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: VCU’s best-known Guaranteed Admission Program is for medicine. The M.D. degree through the VCU School of Medicine offers a strong, innovative medical curriculum that emphasizes both academic study and compassionate patient care, preparing students for the challenges and complexities of medical practice. Guaranteed Admission students who successfully meet all of the requirements of the Guaranteed Admission Program may enter the School of Medicine without further competition. The Guaranteed Admission Program for Medicine is an eight-year program. Students wishing to complete their baccalaureate degrees in fewer than four years will not achieve earlier guaranteed admission into the VCU School of Medicine. Students interested in applying to the Guaranteed Admission Program for Medicine should review the application and admissions process details.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants offered admission prior to May 1 have two weeks to respond to their offer. Applicants offered admission after May 1 have one week to respond to their offer.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: If submitting committee letter or letter packet, no additional letters are required.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters must address personal experiences and characteristics that will help us develop an overall portrait of applicants. A letter based upon direct interaction with applicants that address qualities such as maturity, empathy, character, reliability, interpersonal skills, and any special attributes or experiences will be helpful in the selection process. Letters may be authored by individuals from an academic, clinical, employment, research, or volunteer setting.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: VCU School of Medicine conducts interviews using a virtual Multiple Mini Interview format. Interviews are conducted on select Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and/or Thursdays from August until March.  All information regarding the interview day will be available in the MedAdmit portal for applicants who are selected for interview.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The MMI format is conducted virtually.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
All applicants must have a degree (undergraduate and/or graduate) from a college or university that is accredited in the US or a Canadian equivalent.   

Communication throughout the application process will be made by email through our application portal.

Pre-requisite Courses
Pre-requisite courses are required and must be completed by June 30 of the year of planned matriculation. For a list of current pre-requisites (updated January 2025) please visit: https://medschool.vcu.edu/admissions/prospective/#d.en.650560.  We will not accept on-line course substitutions for science coursework and labs.

P/F Coursework
We require letter grades for any science coursework completed after December 2021.   

MCAT Requirements
We will accept MCAT scores taken in 2024, 2025 and 2026.  The last eligible 2026 date is September 12, 2026.  We will evaluate applications based on the most recent single score or the average of scores for all tests taken within the cycle year (January – September 2026).

CASPer Situational Judgement Assessment
All applicants are required to complete the American Professional Health Sciences (CSP10111) CASPer situational judgment assessment. The last eligible date to take the CASPer assessment for this cycle is September 30, 2026. Reapplicants must complete a new assessment.  Please refer to https://acuityinsights.app for more information.

Letters of Recommendation
For details regarding letters of recommendation, please visit the VCU School of Medicine website: https://medschool.vcu.edu/admissions/prospective/#d.en.650560

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) has established standards regarding the requirement of medical schools to develop and publish technical standards for the admission, retention, and graduation of MD applicants or medical students in accordance with legal requirements and applicable laws. These technical standards ensure that all students, with or without reasonable accommodation, consistently demonstrate the capabilities necessary to meet the academic and clinical requirements of the medical education program. The current technical standards for VCU School of Medicine can be found at the following link: https://assets.som.vcu.edu/pdfs/policies/technical.pdf

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Office of Financial Aid provides individual financial aid counseling and support to all medical students enrolled at VCU School of Medicine. To meet the cost of their medical education, assistance is available in the form of loans and scholarships. Completing FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) is required annually for all students who seek financial aid through federal loans. For need-based scholarship and grant aid, the CSS PROFILE online form should be completed annually as well. This information is used to award grants from the Department of Health and Human Services and institutional need-based aid. Completion of these forms will allow the Office of Financial Aid to give students an accurate picture of what their eligibility for aid will be. For more information on financial aid, please visit the following site: https://medschool.vcu.edu/education/medical-education/financial-aid/

medSchoolPrograms.info: VCU School of Medicine also offers a 3-year Competency Based Graduation (CBG) program to interested students after matriculation. This unique opportunity aims to address the physician workforce shortage in Virginia, as those who stay for residency are more likely to remain in the Commonwealth to practice. For more information about this program, please refer to the following website: https://medschool.vcu.edu/education/medical-education/curriculum/competency-based/

VCU School of Medicine also offers a combined M.D./M.S. program in Clinical Translational Sciences; program details will be provided to interested students after matriculation to VCU School of Medicine.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Although there is no expiration date for prerequisite coursework, we strongly encourage completion of additional science coursework within 4 years of applying to VCU School of Medicine.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Successful applicants to VCU School of Medicine demonstrate exceptional qualities that align with the mission, vision, and values of the institution. Impacting communities through service and hands-on clinical experiences are highly regarded in our selection process in addition to academic metrics.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Successful applicants to VCU School of Medicine are required to complete a minimum of 100 hours of clinical experiences; a minimum of 40 of these hours must be from shadowing. Clinical experiences can include direct hands-on patient care (medical assistant, scribing, nursing care, EMT, etc.) in addition to in-person physician shadowing.
